name: Wall sit
safety: Stop if you feel sharp knee pain. Start with a short hold.
why: Holds your legs in the low ready shape so you can stay down between shots.

name: Sit-low hold
safety: Stop if you feel sharp knee pain. Bend only as far as you can control.
why: Trains the ready stance so your hips stay down while you wait for the next shot.

name: Goblet squat
cues: hold the weight at your chest
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. Start light.
why: Loads the squat so you can sit lower and push back up into a jump.

name: Forward lunge with reach
cues: step out to a length you can hold
front knee stays over the ankle
back knee drops toward the floor
mistakes: stepping so far the heel lifts
safety: Stop if you feel sharp knee or hip pain. Shorten the step if the front heel lifts.
why: Teaches a deep front-court lunge and a long arm reach for a net shot.

name: Pause lunge and recover
cues: lunge and pause at the bottom
return low to a ready stance
mistakes: bouncing out with the back leg only
standing up on the way back
safety: Stop if you feel sharp knee pain. Pause only as low as you can push out of.
why: Builds the push out of a deep lunge so you get back to base before the next shot.

name: Lateral lunge
safety: Stop if you feel sharp hip or knee pain. Start with a short step.
why: Opens the hips for a side step so you can reach a wide shot and stay low.

name: Split-step hops
safety: Stop if you feel sharp ankle or knee pain. Keep the hop small.
why: Builds a small gym rebound so the legs stay springy. Conditioning, not a court-timing drill.

name: Jump rope
cues: hop on the balls of the feet
safety: Stop if you feel sharp ankle or calf pain. Start with a slow turn.
why: Builds bounce and rally stamina so your feet stay quick late in a game.

name: Six-corner shadow
cues: start in a low ready stance
mistakes: standing up on the way back
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. Walk the pattern before you speed up.
why: Practices the path back to base after a corner lunge so you are set for the next shot.

name: Skater hops
cues: stay low, do not stand up
safety: Stop if you feel sharp knee or ankle pain. Start with a short hop.
why: Trains a sideways push so your first step to a wide shot is quick and balanced.

name: Calf raises
cues: rise onto the balls of the feet
safety: Stop if you feel sharp calf or ankle pain. Use a light touch on a wall if you wobble.
why: Strengthens the bounce in your calves so split steps and jumps leave the floor cleanly.

name: Single-leg calf raise
mistakes: dropping the hip on the standing side
safety: Stop if you feel sharp ankle pain. Hold the wall until you are steady.
why: Builds one-leg calf strength so you can push off and land on one foot.

name: Squat jumps
cues: stick the landing before the next jump
safety: Stop if you feel sharp knee pain. Start with a small jump.
why: Builds the leg push that gets you up to a high smash contact.

name: Front plank
cues: do not let the hips sag
safety: Stop if you feel sharp back pain. Drop to your knees if the full plank is too hard.
why: Teaches the trunk to stay still so a swing does not fold you over.

name: Side plank
safety: Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain. Bend the bottom knee if you need to.
why: Builds side trunk strength so you stay balanced on one leg in a lunge.

name: Standing trunk turn
cues: turn the chest, not just the arms
mistakes: turning the feet with the chest
safety: Stop if you feel sharp back pain. Turn only as far as you can stay tall.
why: Trains the trunk turn you use to load a clear and a smash.

name: Band trunk rotation
cues: fix the band to a post at chest height
turn the chest away from the band
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain. Start with a light band.
why: Adds a light pull so your trunk turn stays strong through a smash.

name: Wall angels
cues: back and head on the wall
safety: Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain. Only lift as high as the arms stay on the wall.
why: Opens the shoulders so you can reach a higher contact on the smash.
